notes:
The whole walkthrough arrived inside a single [TABLE] cell with no [n] numbering, so source_bullets refer to the seven top-level '*' bullets in the order they appear in that cell: 1 start with Naiko-Paneiko, 2 the four reporters, 3 return to Naiko-Paneiko, 4 enter Inner Horutoto Ruins from East Sarutabaruta, 5 the Cracked Wall, 6 the Mahogany Door, 7 return to finish. Bullet 2 lists four reporters with no order given and each hands over a DIFFERENT key item, so they are an unordered group of four and each carries its own key item as evidence -- no duplicate-evidence hazard, unlike the seventeen identical Clay Tablets in An Explorer's Footsteps. 'Southern' and 'Northern Windurst Waters' are halves of zone 238, Windurst Waters, so both collapse to that one zone. The Mahogany Door only produces a confirming MESSAGE; it grants nothing, so it carries no evidence -- the Windurst Woods scoop was already obtained from Umumu and belongs there. It is recorded as an item requirement on that step instead, which is what the quest description ('confirm the validity of the scoop reported by the reporter in Windurst Woods') actually asks for. The two bullets under 'After the walkthrough: Notes' are a long essay on why level 79-92 monsters live in a beginner zone and how to avoid aggro; neither is a step, and their (H-8) references are hazards, not destinations. The alternative Cracked Wall at (G-9) is a route around goblin aggro for players with no Invisible, not a second step.

  step 9: It only prints a message confirming the Windurst Woods scoop; nothing is granted, so this step carries no evidence.

notes:
Twenty bullets that are really three actions, all on Faursel in Lower Jeuno: talk, trade, come back tomorrow. Bullets 1 to 4 are one continuous conversation (cutscene, pick the hidden third option, talk again and pick 'I want to go', he lists the four routes), so they merge into step 1 rather than becoming four rungs on the same NPC.

The item requirement is the reason this is medium. Bullets 9-20 sit under three '==' path headings and are a four-way OR whose branches are themselves AND-lists: Advanced is one unnamed beastman-stronghold coffer key (the page names the seven ZONES, never the key items, so hard rule 1 forbids writing 'Davoi Coffer Key') -or- any unnamed testimony -or- all three Pso'Xja chips; Intermediate is Jade Cryptex + Silver Engraving + 13 Knot Quipus; Beginner is all six sub-job quest items; and the fourth route is 500,000 gil, which is not an item at all. items_alt is a flat OR-list of single items and cannot hold an alternative AND-list, so nothing is written into items and items_partial is set instead -- a truthful 'there is a requirement here I cannot express' rather than an arbitrarily chosen path that would mislead every player on the other three. For the record, of the twelve named candidates only 13 Knot Quipus fails to resolve.

The Boarding permit is in the header's Reward, so by hard rule 7 it is not used as evidence on step 3 even though bullet 7 hands it over there. The 'next game day' wait is unobservable and gets a note, not a wait rung with no target and no zone. 'Item Reqs: Tenshodo Membership' has no slot in the schema and does not resolve as a key item; it is flagged and gates nothing. Bullet 8 (go see Naja Salaheem for Aht Urhgan Mission 1) is a pointer at the next content, not a step of this quest, and the Jijiroon note is flavour. The Rhapsodies of Vana'diel Mission 2-5 shortcut ('Where's Tenzen?', free permit) collapses steps 2 and 3 entirely and is recorded on step 1.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: None of this fits items/items_alt, hence items_partial.

steps.note: in Neptune's Spire. Choose the hidden third option at the bottom of the list, talk again and choose 'I want to go'; he then offers the Advanced, Intermediate, Beginner and 500,000 gil routes. If you are on Rhapsodies of Vana'diel Mission 2-5, choosing 'Where's Tenzen?' here gives the Boarding permit outright and the rest of the ladder is skipped.

Trade any ONE of: a coffer key from Davoi, Beadeaux, Castle Oztroja, Temple of Uggalepih, Den of Rancor, Quicksand Caves or Sea Serpent Grotto (the page names only the zones, never the keys); any testimony; Carmine Chip + Cyan Chip + Gray Chip; Jade Cryptex + Silver Engraving + 13 Knot Quipus; or Magicked Skull + Damselfly Worm + Crab Apron + Bloody Robe + Dhalmel Saliva + Wild Rabbit Tail. Paying 500,000 gil replaces the trade entirely and also grants the Map of Wajaom Woodlands and a teleport to the Wajaom Woodlands Leypoint. Coffer keys are 5,000 gil from the Curio Moogle with Rhapsody in Umber, which is what makes 'Advanced' the easy route.

zone out and come back the NEXT GAME DAY, which nothing in the packets reports. He hands over the Boarding permit, which is a header Reward and so is not used as evidence. Afterwards you sail from Mhaura to Al Zahbi (Laughing Bison at Mhaura (I-9) says which port the next ship serves), or skip the boat with a Unity Warp once you hold the permit.

notes:
The opening sentence ('Travel to the Durable Shields shop and speak with Guslam...') sits ABOVE bullet [1] and carries no number, so step 1's source_bullets is deliberately empty rather than borrowing [1], which is the Eldieme trip.

Bullets 1-3 are one action, not three: go to the coffer, open it, receive the key item. The header spells the OR out -- 'Eld. Coffer Key -OR- Thief's Tools' -- and both resolve, so this is a genuine items/items_alt pair rather than the items_partial fudge Under Oath needed for the same shape. Thief's Tools still require Thief as a job, which nothing here can express. The Old gauntlets key item is obtained at that step and is its evidence.

Bullet 5 is explicitly conditional on this being your FIRST artifact set, so Deadly Minnow and Yin Pocanakhu are optional. They are ordered, not a group -- the page says speak to one, then head to Lower Jeuno for the other.

Bullet 10 is a fight and an examine in one sentence ('Once Dark Spark is defeated, examine one of the torches'), so it splits into two rungs sharing bullet 10. ADVERSARY CHANGE: the draft recorded those two rungs as object 'Torch'. The page never writes that name -- it says 'one of the torches', lower case and plural, on a page that capitalises Treasure Coffer, Dark Spark and Magicked astrolabe. That is the guide's 'the baskets' case exactly, so both steps 7 and 9 are now {type: none, name: null} with the reason in each note. Nothing else about those rungs moved: the zone, the grid, the Dark Spark spawn/kill and the Shadow flames evidence all stand, and the ladder is unaffected.

'After the walkthrough: Two Additional Coffers' is NOT part of the ladder and the page says so outright -- the Garlaige Citadel and Castle Oztroja coffers are extra armour pieces, the quest is complete once you have the hands, and the twenty-line Castle Oztroja lever combination table is a door puzzle for those optional coffers. The 2026 wiki note there even contradicts the page's own claim that the quest must be active. None of it is a step.

'Quest Reqs: Must have started Enveloped in Darkness' is a STARTED-not-completed gate; putting it in prev would demand completion and could hide the quest from a player who is correctly eligible, so it is left out and flagged instead. Only the header's Previous field, The Crimson Trial, is recorded.

  step 7: Hard rule 1 and the 'the baskets' precedent make this {none, null}, not an invented 'Torch'.

notes:
Medium because the page is incomplete in a way that cannot be papered over: bullet 3's table says the aid item you pick sets the number of switches -- 3 for the Scope up to 10 for the Costume kit -- but bullet 6 documents only THREE switch locations. The ladder is therefore exactly right for the Scope route and short for every other, which is why the page itself recommends the Scope.

The Temple of the Goddess is not a zone in res/zones.lua; it is a place inside Metalworks (zone 237), which is also where the Cermet Refinery, the Replica and the kiln are, so every step in this quest is in Metalworks.

The seven aid items are a dialogue choice made at the ??? in the same interaction as bullet 2, not a rung of their own, and the page never marks any of them [KI] -- of the seven only 'Costume kit' resolves as a key item and 'Scope' resolves as an unrelated inventory item, so claiming evidence from them would be a guess. They are recorded in the note instead. Bullet 4 is a statement of the objective.

Bullet 5's five clue NPCs have no order and you do not need all of them (Folzen gives the count, the others the order), so they share a group and draw at once; a strict ladder would mark Folzen alone and nothing else. The page gives them prose locations and no grid refs, so grid stays null. Bullet 6's three switches are likewise a group: the order matters intensely but is randomised per play and told to you in game, so no fixed sequence can be written down and all three should draw together. ADVERSARY CHANGE: the draft recorded them as objects 'Small Switch', 'Medium Switch' and 'Large Switch'. The page names them only as 'the small switch', 'the medium switch' and 'the large switch' -- size descriptors on a common noun, capitalised in the draft and nowhere in the source. That is the guide's 'the baskets' case, so all three are now {type: none, name: null}; the rungs, the group, the zone and the grids (G-7, G-8, F-8) are unchanged, only the three names are gone. The generic_npc_name flag is left in place as the pointer to this decision. Quasim is a landmark beside the medium switch, not a target.

Bullet 7's table (Gentle Tiger, Militant Gale, Pensive Beast and Salim himself intercepting you at a switch, and the right answer for each) is failure avoidance, and bullet 8's recovery -- speak to Ferghus then Folzen after Luto or Miledo is captured, quest over if the same one is caught twice -- is a repair path off a mistake, not a rung. Bullet 10 is a once-per-conquest-tally cooldown. The Reward field is a table of seven outcomes keyed to the aid item, not evidence.
